q: You want to record the validation loss after every training epoch so the UI can draw a curve. Which call fits?
e: Metrics can be logged many times; the `step` makes a history. Parameters are immutable within a run and tags are strings.

q: Which call returns the run with the highest `roc_auc` first?
e: Scores sort descending, errors such as RMSE ascending. `get_run` fetches one known run and `last_active_run` is simply the most recent.

q: Autologging is on and you call `model.fit(X_train, y_train)`. What is **not** logged automatically?
o: Metrics on your own held-out validation set
e: Autologging only sees the `fit()` call. Validation metrics on your own data must be computed and logged by you.

q: What does the signature of a logged model describe, and why does it matter?
o: The author of the model; it is needed for audit logs
The input and output schema; it is required to register the model in Unity Catalog
The Python version only; it is used by autologging
e: The signature lists input columns and types and the output type. Unity Catalog requires it, and serving uses it to check requests.

q: A tuning job trains 20 configurations. How do you keep them grouped and still compare each one?
o: Log all 20 results as parameters of one run
Use one parent run and a nested child run per configuration
e: Nested runs carry `mlflow.parentRunId`, so the UI groups them under the parent, while each child keeps its own parameters and metrics.
